newsitem.title: INDIA: India calls for private investment in ports.
newsitem.headline: India calls for private investment in ports.

text.p: Indian Surface Transport Minister T.G. Venkatraman on Thursday urged the private sector to invest actively in the ailing ports sector.
"We are constantly urging upon private parties to come forward and participate actively," Surface Transport minister T.G. Venkatraman told reporters.

He was speaking during the signing of an agreement between Bombay's Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT) and the Nava Sheva International Container Terminal Ltd (NSICT) to set up a two-berth container terrminal.
The minister said the government aimed to sign a privatisation agreement every month in either the ports sector or the roads sector.
"Our objective is to sign one agreement providing for private participation every month," Venkatraman said.
He said the government was planning to double its annual port handling capacity in the next five years from the current 215 million tonnes.
"A significant part of the additional capacity will be in the private sector domain," Venkatraman added without elaborating.
Under the agreement signed on Thursday, NSICT will set up a two-berth container terminal at JNPT costing seven billion rupees ($196 million).
NSICT is a consortium of Australia's P&O Ports, Konsortium Perkapalan Berhad of Malaysia and DBC Port Management Pvt Ltd of India.
Under the contract, NSICT will construct, manage and maintain the terminal for a period of 30 years on a build, operate and transfer basis.
"The project is expected to be ready by 36 months," JNPT chairman R.Vasudevan told the meeting.
Venkatraman said JNPT's container-handling capacity would rise to one million twenty equivalent units (TEUs) from 500,000 TEUs at present after the new terminal started operations.
